questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It takes only a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you start riding.

questions.question: What should you do with your feet while riding?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
Keep them away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag them or point them down, as this can cause injury. Keep them near the controls so you can use them quickly if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT good clothing for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
A baseball cap to cover your hair.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a strong jacket and long pants, sturdy boots that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not protect you during a crash.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: The tread and wear on your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tread and wear on your tires.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, lights, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Do not allow passengers on your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to prevent head and neck injuries if you crash.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers can be slippery. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when riding?

options.text: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes less effectively than eyeglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to increase your speed.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement gives the best grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers all reduce traction and are more dangerous for motorcycles.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
It does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet does not limit your side vision. A Department of Transportation-approved helmet allows you to see as well as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: During a pre-ride check, make sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes rub against the steering.
Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can stop the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Downshifting to a lower gear is also called:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows the motorcycle, similar to braking. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have had too much to drink. Do what you can to stop them, including taking their keys if needed. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, ride in the center of the lane. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors, so this position helps you stay visible.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all hazardous. Dry pavement is safest.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go through it as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Riding next to a car:

options.text: Can put you in their blind spot.
Is only risky on wet roads.
Makes it easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in their blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route.

questions.question: Your body removes alcohol only through:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. There are no quick ways to sober up.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: Stopping will be harder than normal.
You want to view the scenery.
You want other drivers to cut in front of you.
You want the driver ahead to not know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will be harder than normal.
questions.explanation: You need extra space when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility ahead, or heavy traffic where drivers may cut in front of you. Keep a larger following distance in these situations.

questions.question: If you think your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay farther behind other vehicles on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle takes longer to stop, give yourself more space.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars do. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Slow down so other vehicles can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: You cannot see blind spots by just using your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection when riding.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, the laces should:
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoe laces securely so they do not get caught on your motorcycle.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: You cannot see as well ahead.
It makes it harder to see the other vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see better ahead and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane.
